edges.description: Core-Mediator dysfunction disrupts neurodevelopmental transcriptional programs, with particular impact on cerebellar development.
Disrupted neuronal developmental programs contribute to intellectual disability.
Disrupted motor developmental programs contribute to axial hypotonia with distal spasticity.
Disrupted basal ganglia/cerebellar circuits contribute to dystonic movements.
Impaired cerebellar development produces cerebellar hypoplasia.
Disrupted lens developmental programs contribute to cataracts in severely affected individuals.

nodes.description: MED27 is a subunit of the structural core of the Mediator complex. Biallelic variants disrupt core-Mediator-dependent transcription of developmental gene-expression programs. The homogeneous phenotype and multiple biallelic families support a critical role for MED27 in normal human neural development, particularly for the cerebellum. MED27 belongs to the group of Mediator complex-associated disease genes.
